14:Pit is distributed from GitHub (`main` and tagged releases) and is intentionally not published to npm.
15-
16-## Set up
17-
18-```sh
19-git clone https://github.com/cv/pit.git
20-cd pit
21-npm install
22-```
23-
24-Load local source for interactive development:
25-
26-```sh
27-pi --no-extensions -e ./src/index.ts
28-```
29-
30-`--no-extensions` disables discovered and configured extensions while the explicit `-e` loads this checkout. This avoids accidentally testing an installed copy alongside local source. See the [native runtime guide](native/wasmtime-executor/README.md) if you need to build or smoke-test the addon itself.
31-
32-## Make changes
33-
34-Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing source boundaries. Keep implementation in the domain that owns the behavior and avoid general-purpose utility modules.
35-
36-Project-persisted workflow helpers live in `.pi/functions/`; their location determines scope. Their [local guide](.pi/functions/README.md) explains the repository's helper boundaries. They are optional conveniences: the commands below work without enabling project functions.
37-
38-Pit is 0.x. A breaking change removes the old name, field, path, or behavior outright: do not add deprecated aliases, compatibility shims, dual readers, or migration code. Record the break in `CHANGELOG.md`.
39-
40-When changing global function definitions, regenerate the contract:
41-
42-```sh
43-npm run globals:generate
44-```
--
71:- `docs/security.md`: threat model and runtime guarantees; `SECURITY.md` owns reporting and supported-release policy.
72-- `docs/architecture.md`: internal components, invariants, and source ownership.
73:- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: the human contributor path; `docs/releasing.md` owns release procedure.
74-- `AGENTS.md` and `.pi/skills/`: agent instructions and detailed workflows, not the sole home of essential human contribution requirements.
75-- Subsystem READMEs: local build instructions and subsystem-specific conventions.
76:- `CHANGELOG.md`: release changes; case studies: historical experience, clearly separated from current reference.
77-
78:Add new pages to the [documentation index](docs/README.md), check relative links and moved heading links, and avoid duplicating version numbers or method signatures unnecessarily. See the [release guide](docs/releasing.md) for publication and installed-tag verification.
79-
80-## Pull requests
81-
82-- Keep each pull request focused and explain user-visible behavior.
83-- Include tests for success, failure, cancellation, and boundary cases where applicable.
84-- Update the relevant user guide, reference, architecture, or security document when behavior changes.
85-- Do not edit `src/generated/global-contract.d.ts` manually.
86-- Keep generated files, dependency changes, and lockfile changes intentional.
87-- Confirm that no secrets, credentials, private paths, or unsanitized session data are included.
88-
89-Report vulnerabilities privately according to [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), not through a pull request or public issue.

2095356 feat(durable): hide pi-durable's coding tools from the model, honoring allowedTools

On pi-durable hosts Pit now wraps read, write, edit, bash, and powershell
so the model is offered only typescript, as on Pi. allowedTools from the
user's and a trusted project's pit.json keeps matches offered, and the new
hideTools option replaces the list or turns hiding off. tools.* no longer
binds the file and shell tools that workspace.* and shell.* supersede.

Refs #356
4428593 ci: let pi-action's App token update workflows

The token lacked the `workflows` permission, so pi's push of
.github/workflows/pi-assistant.yml was rejected (#355).
70f1a86 ci: run pi-action 2.4.0 with pit 0.35.1
